records.label: Brain
records.guide: Attention, memory, habit, emotion, and learning loops.
records.notice: The brain learns what you repeat, not what you meant to repeat.
records.tryThis: Choose one tiny movement and repeat it slowly ten times.
records.apply: Play open → fret 2 → open on one string. Keep the timing even.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: neuroscience of practice, myelin, deliberate practice.

records.label: Hands
records.guide: Fingers, tendons, nerves, dexterity, and safe movement.
records.notice: Tension in one finger often spreads into the whole hand.
records.tryThis: Lift one finger slowly while the others stay relaxed. Make the movement smaller if the hand locks.
records.apply: Play a 1-2-3-4 chromatic pattern slowly. Aim for quiet fingers, not speed.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: hand anatomy, tendon care, classical technique.

records.label: Ears
records.guide: Listening, pitch, rhythm perception, and audiation.
records.notice: Your ear starts learning before your fingers know what to do.
records.tryThis: Sing one note, then find it on the guitar.
records.apply: Play two notes and decide which one feels like home.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: ear training, audiation, music cognition.

records.label: Eyes
records.guide: Pattern recognition, notation, tab, and fretboard maps.
records.notice: The eye turns repeated shapes into maps.
records.tryThis: Look at a simple tab pattern and trace where it lives on the guitar before playing.
records.apply: Read 0-2-0 on one string, then play it while watching the fretboard.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: visual learning, notation, fretboard mapping.

records.label: Breath / Body
records.guide: Posture, relaxation, body scan, and nervous system regulation.
records.notice: If the breath locks, the hands usually tighten too.
records.tryThis: Exhale before changing chords. Notice whether the hand softens.
records.apply: Play Am slowly while breathing out before each change.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: posture, relaxation, somatic learning.

records.label: Heart / Feeling
records.guide: Motivation, confidence, shame, joy, identity, and expression.
records.notice: Feeling is not separate from learning. It changes what the body allows.
records.tryThis: Record one imperfect take and listen for one thing that worked.
records.apply: End practice with one musical conversation, even if it is messy.
records.sourceNote: Future source notes: performance psychology, motivation, reflective practice.
